@typescript-eslint/no-duplicate-type-con.whyOxlintLines: oxlint reports the primitive intersection (string & string) but not the structurally identical object literals on the next line; ESLint asks the type checker and catches both. Measured: with this rule enabled alone, oxlint reports `string & string` and `string | string` (the latter only with ignoreUnions off, so the option is honoured) and stays silent on `{a: string} | {a: string}` and `{b: string} & {b: string}`.
